pairs.difference: A: the hat is one orange-brown mass with a red band on a saturated blue sunburst. Its shadow side shifts to a muted mauve-brown, so the card is basically one warm hue against one cool hue, like the generated glove in the lessons. B: the jacket mixes a muted beige body, orange trim, a dark green sash and yellow badges on green, which is a broader and more natural palette. Numbers for both cards are in the real range, so this rests on the eye.
pairs.fix: Make the hat a dusty, desaturated tan felt with some grey-brown in it, not bright orange. Let the shadow under the brim go a deep cool brown. Make the hatband a muted dark red.

pairs.difference: A: the background is acid lime-green (chroma 0.194, above the real range). The rope and sand are the same warm tan-orange, with almost no neutral or third hue (2.27 hue families, below the real range). The only accent is a tiny red ring. B: a red mower, a cyan background, green grass and grey-black wheels give clear hue roles and some neutral rest. Its low shadow-chroma number comes from the dark tyres, which is believable local color.
pairs.fix: Tone the background down to a softer, less acid green. Give the rope a paler natural fibre colour with grey-beige in its shadows, and make the sand a cooler, lighter beige so rope and ground don't merge into one orange.

pairs.difference: B: a saturated magenta background (chroma 0.258, well above the real range) sits behind a star that is all one yellow-gold. There is no neutral anywhere, and the gold shadows only darken to orange. A: the umbrella's red and yellow panels sit on cyan, with a grey-white pole as a neutral rest. Its chroma levels match the real cards.
pairs.fix: Tone the magenta background down to a softer violet-pink. Draw the badge as polished gold with pale near-white highlights and cool brown-olive shadows, plus a little grey metal at the rivets.

pairs.difference: A: an orange-yellow sunburst, orange sand and a yellow-green cactus pull the whole card warm (warm share 0.78). The cactus green itself leans olive-yellow, and the sand's shadows go to orange-brown. B: the yellow duck sits on a cool green background with a blue base and grey spring, so warm and cool are separated as in the real sunscreen card.
pairs.fix: Use a cooler background, such as teal or sky blue, behind the cactus. Make the cactus a fresh blue-green with cool green shadows rather than olive-yellow, and keep the sand pale and lightly warm.

pairs.difference: A: a pink tray, blue ice and an orange table on a cyan sunburst give a busy but readable set of hue roles. B: a fruit plate on a warm wooden table with many pure fruit hues and low background chroma. Each sits at one edge of the real ranges (A on hue count, B on warm share), but neither shows the warm cream neutrals or one-hue saturation seen in the lessons.

B: a grey horseshoe (subject chroma 0.05, below the real range) sits between a loud magenta background (0.213) and an orange wood shelf. The card is 89% warm and the subject has no local colour of its own, so the background does all the work. A: blue sneakers with green and orange accents on an orange and cream set have a clear hero against background.
pairs.fix: Draw the horseshoe as warm-grey iron with faint bluish highlights. Make the backdrop a softer, less saturated colour, and give the shelf a muted brown wood so the card is not mostly magenta and orange.

pairs.difference: Both cards are very warm (about 0.80 warm share, above the real range). A: the sky, mesas, sand, wood and fire all sit in one pink-orange family. Shadows under the stones and pot go to dull red-brown (shadow-chroma 0.59, below the real range), and the black pot is the only neutral. B: the orange pump has a cream and grey trim and a cool lavender sky, so there is more hue separation.
pairs.fix: Make the sky a clearer cool blue-violet and the stones a cool grey. Let the shadows under the logs and pot stay a rich deep purple-brown rather than muddy orange-red.

pairs.difference: A: the saloon walls, porch, ground and mesas are all the same orange-tan (warm share 0.75, above the real range). Only the sky is cool, and the blue windows are tiny, so there is no muted or neutral area to rest the eye. B: the dock wood and red ring are clearly separated from a large teal water mass, with white ring bands as neutrals.
pairs.fix: Paint the saloon in weathered grey-brown wood with some faded painted trim, such as a muted green or cream. Make the ground a paler, cooler sand, so the building and the desert are not one orange mass.

pairs.difference: B: the wagon's canvas cover is a warm cream-yellow rather than a cool off-white, the same warm-neutral drift as the generated computers in the lessons. The wood and red wheel rims add more orange, and the shadows under the wagon go a flat brown (shadow-chroma 0.64, low). A: the orange wooden boat sits on a strong cyan water mass with green lily pads, so the hue roles are clear.
pairs.fix: Make the canvas cover a cool off-white with light blue-grey shadows. Make the wheel rims a muted dark red, and let the shadow under the wagon be a cool green-brown on the grass.

pairs.difference: A: the saddle is saturated orange-brown leather on a red pad and orange wood beam against blue (2.72 hue families, below the real range). It has the same pushed orange leather as the generated gloves, and the metal stirrups are the only neutral. B: the fountain's cream stone, cyan water, yellow stripes and a terracotta floor are more varied. The cream stone is warm, but the lesson real cards also hold warm grounds.
pairs.fix: Draw the saddle in a deeper, less orange chestnut leather with dark cool-brown shadows. Make the saddle pad a muted burgundy or blanket pattern and the beam a pale grey-tan wood.

pairs.difference: A: the boots are rust-brown on an orange and yellow striped background (warm share 0.99, far above the real range of up to 0.73, and 2.17 hue families). The only cool note is the thin turquoise stitching, and the boot shadows go a reddish brown. B: coral flip-flops with yellow straps on teal stripes form a clear warm-on-cool hero and background.
pairs.fix: Put the boots on a cool background, such as teal, sky-blue or violet stripes. Keep the leather a natural mid-brown with cool dark-brown shadows and a little grey-silver on the spurs.

pairs.difference: B: the caravan body is a warm cream-yellow instead of a white, the warm-neutral drift seen in the generated computers. It sits on a loud violet background (chroma 0.199, above the real range) above yellow-green grass. A: the red guitar on a blue stage with spotlights is busy (6.46 hue families, at the top of the range). Its stage blues are muted, though, and its white pickguard reads as a true neutral.
pairs.fix: Paint the caravan body a clean cool white with light blue-grey shadows. Tone the violet background down to a softer lilac, and make the grass a natural mid green rather than yellow-green.

pattern: The lessons show generated cards turning white and grey objects warm cream or beige (computer, lighthouse stone, wagon canvas, caravan). They also push leather to one saturated orange (glove, saddle, boots, hat) and pull the whole card into one warm family where subject, ground and background share the same orange-tan, leaving little cool neutral rest. The real cards keep cool off-white or grey neutrals, shadows that go a cool, related brown or violet, and a clear warm hero on a cool background (or the reverse). Backgrounds that are pure loud magenta, lime or orange behind a single-hue subject are another giveaway.
